what: Demonstration with the daily french births
title: Seasonal Adjustment of High Frequency Data with JDemetra+ 3.x
text: Plot raw series: Preparation calendar package rjd3toolkit: Creation calendar regressor matrix package rjd3toolkit: Preprocessing function fractionalAirlineEstimation:   Decomposition AMB (Arima Model Based) algorithm: Plot:   Perform Arima Model Based (AMB) decomposition several periodcities : Plot comparison two AMB methods annual periodicity:  package rjd3x11plus, can perform X-11 like decomposition (non integer) periodicity.
code: library("rjd3highfreq") #>  #> Attaching package: 'rjd3highfreq' #> The following object is masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     loess ## Import of data df_daily <- read.csv2("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TanguyBarthelemy/Tsace_RJD_Webinar_Dec22/b5fcf6b14ae47393554950547ef4788a0068a0f6/Data/TS_daily_births_franceM_1968_2020.csv")  # Creation of log variables to multiplicative model df_daily$log_births <- log(df_daily$births) df_daily$date <- as.Date(df_daily$date) # French calendar frenchCalendar <- rjd3toolkit::national_calendar(days = list(   rjd3toolkit::fixed_day(7, 14), # Bastille Day   rjd3toolkit::fixed_day(5, 8, validity = list(start = "1982-05-08")), # End of 2nd WW   rjd3toolkit::special_day('NEWYEAR'),   rjd3toolkit::special_day('MAYDAY'), # 1st may   rjd3toolkit::special_day('EASTERMONDAY'),   rjd3toolkit::special_day('ASCENSION'),   rjd3toolkit::special_day('WHITMONDAY'),   rjd3toolkit::special_day('ASSUMPTION'),   rjd3toolkit::special_day('ALLSAINTSDAY'), # Toussaint   rjd3toolkit::special_day('ARMISTICE'), # End of 1st WW   rjd3toolkit::special_day('CHRISTMAS')) ) # Calendar regressor matrix cal_reg <- rjd3toolkit::holidays(     calendar = frenchCalendar,     start = "1968-01-01", length = nrow(df_daily),     type = "All", nonworking = 7L)  colnames(cal_reg) <- c("14th_july", "8th_may", "1st_jan", "1st_may",                        "east_mon", "asc", "pen_mon",                        "15th_aug", "1st_nov", "11th_nov", "Xmas") pre_pro <- fractional_airline_estimation(     series = df_daily$births,     xreg = cal_reg,     period = 7, # weekly frequency     outliers = c("ao", "wo"), log = TRUE, series_time = df_daily$date)  print(pre_pro) #>  #>  #> Fractional Airline estimation: #>  #>   period           : 7.000 #>   series_time      : 1968-01-01,  ..., 2020-12-31 #>   parameters       : 0.762, 0.973 #>   t                : 136.884, 774.367 #>   score            : 2.088, 24.448 #>   covariance       : [0.000, 0.000], [0.000, 0.000] #>   log              : TRUE #>  #>  #> Regression results: #>  #>                    coef        t #>   -------------  ------  ------- #>   14th_july      -0.123  -26.062 #>   8th_may        -0.142  -26.342 #>   1st_jan        -0.222  -47.351 #>   1st_may        -0.122  -26.264 #>   east_mon       -0.189  -40.764 #>   asc            -0.173  -37.195 #>   pen_mon        -0.190  -40.943 #>   15th_aug       -0.118  -25.346 #>   1st_nov        -0.150  -32.566 #>   11th_nov       -0.124  -26.814 #>   Xmas           -0.231  -49.744 #>   WO.1999-12-31  -0.176   -7.792 #>   AO.1995-08-15  -0.222   -6.550 #>   WO.1999-12-24  -0.145   -6.398 #>   AO.2012-01-01   0.210    6.179 #>   AO.1998-07-14  -0.210   -6.188 #>   AO.1997-07-14  -0.209   -6.160 #>   AO.1995-05-01  -0.204   -6.015 #>  #>  #> Likelihood: #>  #>   ll               : 36823.915 #>   ssq              : 25.169 #>   nobs             : 19359.000 #>   neffectiveobs    : 19351.000 #>   nparams          : 21.000 #>   df               : 19330.000 #>   aic              : -73605.830 #>   aicc             : -73605.782 #>   bic              : -73440.549 #>   bic2             : -3.795 #>   bicc             : -6.635 #>   hannanquinn      : -73551.669 plot(pre_pro, main = "French births") plot(x = pre_pro,      from = as.Date("2000-01-01"), to = as.Date("2000-12-31"),      main = "French births in 2000") #> Warning in plot.xy(xy.coords(x, y), type = type, ...): "from" is not a #> graphical parameter #> Warning in plot.xy(xy.coords(x, y), type = type, ...): "to" is not a graphical #> parameter # Decomposition with weekly pattern amb.dow <- rjd3highfreq::fractional_airline_decomposition(     series = pre_pro$decomposition$linearized, # linearized series from preprocessing     period = 7,     log = TRUE, series_time = df_daily$date)  # Extract day-of-year pattern from day-of-week-adjusted linearised data amb.doy <- rjd3highfreq::fractional_airline_decomposition(     series = amb.dow$decomposition$sa, # DOW-adjusted linearised data     period = 365.2425, # day of year pattern     log = TRUE, series_time = df_daily$date) plot(amb.dow) plot(amb.doy) amb.multi <- rjd3highfreq::multi_airline_decomposition(   series = pre_pro$decomposition$linearized, # input time series   period = c(7, 365.2425), # 2 frequency   log = TRUE, series_time = df_daily$date) plot(amb.multi)

text: series Numeric vector containing time series modelled. period Numeric vector periods present data. example, c(7, 365.25) weekly annual seasonality. differencing Differencing order apply. default value -1 activates automatic computation. ar Logical. what: Outlier Detection for Extended Airline Models — find_outliers
title: Outlier Detection for Extended Airline Models — find_outliers
text: internal function performs automatic outlier detection high-frequency time series using Extended Airline models.

title: Outlier Detection for Extended Airline Models — find_outliers
code: find_outliers(   input,   types = c("AO"),   start = 0,   end = 0,   critical_value = 0,   max_outliers = 30,   max_round = 30,   precision = 1e-05,   deps = 1e-04 )

title: Outlier Detection for Extended Airline Models — find_outliers
text: input time series types Character vector specifying types outliers detect. Default: c("AO") (additive outliers ). Common options include: "AO" - Additive Outlier "LS" - Level Shift "WO" - Switch Outlier start Integer specifying starting position (1-based R indexing) outlier detection. Default: 0 (detection beginning series). end Integer specifying ending position (1-based R indexing) outlier detection. Default: 0 (detection end series). critical_value Numeric value critical value threshold. Uses maximum value among specified value global max-t threshold based extreme-value theory, roughly order sqrt(2 * log(n))). Default: 0 (global max-t threshold used). max_outliers Integer specifying maximum number outliers detect. Default: 30. max_round Integer specifying maximum number detection iterations. Default: 30. precision Numeric value specifying tolerance convergence optimization algorithms. Default: 1e-5. deps Numeric scalar. Step computation numerical derivatives, used optimisation routine. Default:1e-4.

title: Outlier Detection for Extended Airline Models — find_outliers
text: numeric matrix dimensions [number outliers detected × 2].

title: Outlier Detection for Extended Airline Models — find_outliers
text: Outlier critical value using Ljung algorithm given Ljung, G. M. (1993). outlier detection time series. Journal Royal Statistical Society B 55, 559-567. Solution proposed Brian Monsell (LBS), January 2022

title: Modified X-11 seasonal adjustment — x11plus
text: series Input time series. period Seasonal periodicity series. Must positive real number larger equal 2. multiplicative Decomposition mode series (Boolean). TRUE (default), series decomposed multiplicative trend-cyclical, seasonal, irregular components; FALSE, decomposed additive unobserved components. trend_horizon Bandwidth symmetric local polynomial regression filter. Default 6, giving 13-term filter. See details. trend_degree Polynomial degree preserved symmetric local polynomial regression filter. Default 3, giving preservation cubic polynomials. See details. trend_kernel kernel defining weights objective function. See details. trend_asymmetric Approach deriving asymmetric local polynomial regression filters. See details. trend_coefs filter bank containing weights symmetric trend-cycle filter asymmetric variants. Can object class "list", "matrix", "lp_filter" "rkhs_filter". See details. seas_s0 \(3 \times k\) seasonal filter preliminary seasonal estimation (B5, C5, D5). Default \(3 \times 3\). seas_s1 \(3 \times k\) seasonal filter refined final seasonal estimation (B10, C10, D10). Default \(3 \times 5\). extreme_lsig Lower \(\sigma\)-limit extreme-value correction seasonal-irregular component. Must non-negative, default 1.5. extreme_usig Upper \(\sigma\)-limit extreme-value correction seasonal-irregular component. Must greater extreme_lsig, default 2.5. user_defined vector containing additional output tables. Default NULL.

title: Modified X-11 seasonal adjustment — x11plus
text: object class "hf_decomposition". contains specified parameters matrix stores input series final estimates seasonally adjusted series (D11), trend-cyclical component (D12), seasonal component (D10), irregular component (D13).

title: Modified X-11 seasonal adjustment — x11plus
text: main novelty modified X-11 method implementation advanced options refined final trend-cycle estimation (B7, C7, D7, D12), generalising use classical Henderson filters. following logic applies, see also Webel (2026) Webel Smyk (2024) technical details: trend_coefs unspecified (default), local polynomial regression filters suggested Proietti Luati (2008) applied. underlying regression model, symmetric trend-cycle filter arises, specified trend_horizon, trend_degree, trend_kernel parameters: 2 * trend_horizon + 1 number observations considered local trend approximation , hence, length resulting symmetric trend-cycle filter. trend_degree order polynomial local trend approximation. trend_kernel kernel function defines sequence non-negative weights objective function, minimised respect regression parameters. addition, trend_asymmetric defines method used deriving requisite asymmetric local polynomial regression filters. Three methods currently available: cut--normalise approach Gasser Müller (1979) (CutAndNormalize), direct asymmetric filters suggested Proietti Luati (2008) (Direct), minimum mean squared revision error approach developed Grun-Rehomme et al. (2018) (MMSRE). trend_coefs specified, parameters related trend-cycle estimation ignored, provided trend-cycle filter bank applied. Note rjd3filters package can used create filters, e.g. setting trend_coefs = rjd3filters::rkhs_filter(). Two final warnings regarding seasonal estimation. Extremes seasonal-irregular component currently corrected iterations B C, moving irregular standard deviation always calculated 5-year moving windows. , final replacement values (D9) currently computed. Users must specify seasonal filters seas_s0 seas_s1 match length series, currently automatic resetting ill-specified seasonal filters. , specification seasonal filters long given series simply produce error message.
